headline: The two 'source-mux producers' are NOT device parsers and NOT normalized-state copiers. They are 30/32-byte switch tables that INJECT pre-canned synthetic axis constants into the candidate buffer. Neither one writes LT or RT.

producer_A.selector: r0 = r0 & 0xf; r0 += -1; if (r0 > 9) default; tbb [r0]  - the LOW nibble minus one indexes a 10-entry table
producer_A.fields_written: candidate +0x04 and +0x06 (axis #1 and axis #2) as u32 or s16 stores
producer_A.fields_NOT_written: LT (+0x0c) and RT (+0x0d) - no store to either offset anywhere in the function
producer_A.value_set: 0x0000, 0x8000, 0x7fff, and s16 pairs +/-0x2582 (the 32-bit constants decompose into two s16: 0x5a7e = +0x2582, 0xa582 = -0x2582)

producer_B.selector: r0 = r0 & 0xf0; r0 += -0x10; r0 = r0 >> 4; if (r0 > 9) default; tbb [r0]  - the HIGH nibble minus one indexes the table

answers_to_the_brief.does_producer_A_write_RT: NO - proven by exhaustive read of all 12 instructions; no store targets +0x0c or +0x0d
answers_to_the_brief.selector_low_nibble: a MODE/pattern id (values 1..10), not a device id: the low nibble minus one indexes a 10-entry table of canned axis values for axes #1/#2
answers_to_the_brief.selector_high_nibble: the same kind of mode id for axes #3/#4
answers_to_the_brief.architectural_conclusion: this is a SYNTHETIC INPUT / TEST-PATTERN INJECTOR, not an input-source mux. Calling it a device/source mux was a misreading of the selector - the values written are constants, not copies of any source structure.
answers_to_the_brief.why_the_synthetic_values_matter: 0x8000 is the centre of a 16-bit axis, 0x7fff full-scale, and +/-0x2582 is a fixed partial deflection, so the table produces recognisable canned stick positions. The nested arms also call/goto 0x1e0a61c, 0x1e0a82c, 0x1e0a220 (A) and 0x1e0a682, 0x1e0a892, 0x1e0a286 (B), i.e. other canned-vector tables, consistent with a pattern generator rather than a parser.
answers_to_the_brief.what_this_does_to_the_RT_question: it REMOVES the previous best hypothesis. The mux does not touch LT/RT, so it cannot explain the RT live observation in either direction.

facts: the candidate buffer at sp+1080 is seeded at +0x0c/+0x0d from packed bits 8 and 9 at 0x1e0da54/0x1e0da62, which makes those two bytes DIGITAL by construction on this path
no other store in the region 0x1e0ac14-0x1e0f154 writes +0x0c/+0x0d except that seeding
the same buffer is referenced at 0x1e0cd24, 0x1e0db90, 0x1e0e29c, 0x1e0e2bc, 0x1e0e3c6 and 0x1e0e3d6 and those sites are NOT yet analysed
rt_status.implication: if +0x0c/+0x0d really are digital only, then the D2 14-byte frame carries DIGITAL LT/RT, and the live 0..255 analogue values seen in bytes [15]/[16] must come from a different report path (for example the 28-byte variant or another builder). That would be a significant correction to the live field map - but it is NOT proven yet and must not be stated as fact.
rt_status.next: analyse the remaining buffer references (0x1e0e29c / 0x1e0e2bc / 0x1e0e3c6 / 0x1e0e3d6 in particular, they sit next to the second report variant) and check whether an analogue LT/RT write exists there.
